new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngochang is a tone language (three tones 54/3/31 on unchecked syllables, high/low register on checked). Words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables: full consonant-initial syllables (CV, CVC, CVVC, CVCC) are stressed and obligatorily bear tone; an optional presyllable (V or CV, often reduced to schwa) is unstressed. So in presyllable + full-syllable words prominence is on the final (major) syllable. Placement of stress among full syllables in compounds/polysyllables is not described; the authors explicitly leave stress outside the study.
new_statements.exceptions: None; authors flag stress as outside the scope of the preliminary study and needing work to establish breath groups (fn. 6).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology from a 430-item elicited word list (citation forms), speakers from the Myitkyina area, Kachin State. Statement concerns syllable types (stressed full syllable vs unstressed presyllable), not a phrase-level rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Inglis & Inglis 2003 describes Ngochang as spoken around Myitkyina, Kachin State, Myanmar, i.e. exactly ngoc1235 (Glottolog dialect-level languoid under Achang, ISO acn shared with acha1249). A sibling check filed the same Inglis text under acha1249 (Longchuan Achang); for the catalog it belongs to ngoc1235, while Dai & Cui 1985 (Husa, Longchuan) is the acha1249 description. Speakers report Ngochang and China-side Achang to be 'the same language' (Sampu et al. 2005: v) but no survey has established the dialect relationship.
